---
title: "GitHub in Joma: one app for identity, backup and new machines"
date: 2026-11-26
lang: en
---

This replaces two earlier discussions (identity, 2026-11-18; backup, 2026-11-23), which
disagreed on the main point: an *OAuth App* with the `gist` scope against a *GitHub App*.
Here it is one GitHub App for everything, and the pieces are designed together. The
answer already given (one normal password for all accounts) is carried over. Earlier pages still apply: the [mock-ups of every screen](https://claude.ai/artifact/LjmK3ewEgtoqeJS1XiMg5y)
and the [backup simulation](https://claude.ai/artifact/DrMUQ2mQoNwUtjggqDQjfe).

**The idea in one line.** One "sign in with GitHub" gives three things: a badge that shows
contacts which GitHub account is behind a Jami account, an encrypted backup of your
accounts in a private repo, and a way to get your accounts onto a new or reinstalled
machine without the old one.

**Everything also from the command line** (user, 2026-11-26): an agent should be able to
do all of it, so each piece ships with its `joma` command in the same change (section E).

**What lives where.**

- A public gist `joma.json` in your GitHub account: `{"joma":1, "github_id":<n>, "accounts":[{"jami":"<id>", "label":"…"}]}`.
  Only you can write it. It says which Jami accounts are yours. No secrets.
- A line `X-JOMA-GITHUB:<login>` in each verified account's Jami profile (vCard). Only
  that Jami account can send it. Contacts' Joma matches it against the gist by the
  numeric `github_id`, so a renamed or re-registered login does not fool it. No signing,
  no keys: the two claims name each other.
- A private repo `joma-backup`: one encrypted file per account (Jami's own account
  archive from `exportToFile`, which Joma accounts write *unencrypted*, so Joma encrypts
  it: age-style, scrypt or Argon2 from your password) and an `index.json` (labels, Jami
  IDs, dates; no secrets).
- On the machine: nothing, unless you turn on automatic backups (then a refresh token in
  the system keyring).

**Checked in libjami** (`upstream/jami-daemon`):

- The profile travels as the file it is (`sendProfile`, `data_transfer.cpp:945`);
  `updateProfile` keeps unknown lines and resends to every contact. The key must not
  start with `FN` or `PHOTO` (`removeByKey` matches by prefix).
- Linking a device rebuilds the profile from name and photo only (`jamiaccount.cpp:1479`):
  the line is dropped there, so Joma puts it back.
- Import is `addAccount` with `Account.archivePath`; importing signs a new device
  certificate (`onArchiveLoaded`, `archive_account_manager.cpp:1259`), the same path
  linking takes. So the backup can add a machine while the old one still works.
- Conversation history is not in the archive; it comes back from contacts and your other
  devices.
- `sendTrustRequest` carries a payload (under 64 KB) that arrives with the request.

**Checked in GitHub's docs** (2026-11-26):

- GitHub Apps support the device flow once it is enabled in the app's settings, with the
  client ID only (no client secret, so no server and nothing secret in the binary).
- A user access token has only the permissions both you and the app have, and reaches
  only the repos the app was given.
- Gists are an account permission of GitHub Apps ("Gists", write: create and delete).
  Read from a summary of the docs page, so to confirm when the app exists.
- Tokens expire after 8 hours by default, with a 6-month refresh token; with the device
  flow, refreshing needs no client secret. Expiry can be turned off (not proposed).
- You can revoke the app's authorization from your GitHub settings at any time.
- Not settled by the docs: whether the app's token may *create* the `joma-backup` repo,
  and whether a repo it creates joins the app's "selected repositories". To test (see 3).

## A. The GitHub App

# 1. The app itself

Proposal: one GitHub App "Joma", registered by you under your account, public (anyone
can sign in with it). Device flow on, no webhook, no server; the client ID ships in the
binary. Permissions:

- account: **Gists** read and write (the identity gist);
- repository: **Contents** read and write, plus the required **Metadata** read, on
  *only* `joma-backup` (you pick that one repo when installing).

Nothing else: no email, no other repos, no organizations.

- [ ] A:

# 2. When `gh` is already logged in

Omarchy users often have `gh`. Its token usually has the `repo` and `gist` scopes, which
cover everything here without the app, but reach every repo you have. Proposal: if `gh`
is logged in, Joma offers it ("use your gh login") and otherwise uses the app. Joma never
copies the `gh` token anywhere; it runs `gh api` each time. The alternative is the app
always, so Joma's own access stays narrow.

- [ ] A:

# 3. Creating the backup repo

GitHub's docs don't say whether a GitHub App token may create a repo, or whether a repo
it creates is added to the app's selected repos. Proposal: with `gh`, Joma creates the
private repo itself. Without it, Joma opens `github.com/new` filled in (`joma-backup`,
private), then the app's install page to pick that repo. I test the shorter path when the
app exists and keep it if it works.

- [ ] A:

# 4. Tokens

Proposal: by default Joma keeps no token. It signs in, does the job (publish the gist,
push a backup, restore) and drops the token. Only automatic backups (see 9) keep a
refresh token, in the system keyring, refreshed without a secret; turning them off
deletes it. Revoking the app on GitHub stops everything; Joma then shows "GitHub access
was removed" once.

- [ ] A:

## B. Identity

# 5. Setup, in one go with the backup

Proposal: one "Connect GitHub" on the account row in the accounts tab (and on the
first-start screen). One sign-in, then two switches, both explained: *show a ✓ GitHub
badge to contacts* (makes the link between your GitHub and this Jami account public) and
*back up this account* (private). Either can be on alone. The earlier proposal was a
separate "verify with GitHub" button.

- [ ] A:

# 6. The badge: style, where it shows, requests

Proposal, as in the mock-ups: a check and `github.com/alice` in muted text in the
conversation header and on the account row; a check on the avatar's corner in the chats
and contacts lists, incoming requests and the add card. Joma sends its profile with
contact requests (`sendTrustRequest` payload), so the badge shows before you accept. The
compact bar panel and the call overlay: optional. Keep the Jami picture, link to the
GitHub profile; no GitHub avatar.

- [ ] A:

# 7. Adding contacts by GitHub name

Proposal: a switch above the add input (Jami name or ID / GitHub, Tab flips) plus
`gh:alice` as a shortcut. Joma reads alice's public `joma.json`; with several accounts
listed you pick one by its label. A card shows what was found; nothing is sent until you
confirm.

- [ ] A:

# 8. Re-checking, changes and removal

Proposal: re-check every 3 days and whenever a profile arrives, cached (GitHub allows 60
calls an hour without a login). A missing gist removes the badge with one system line.
If a GitHub account later names a different Jami ID than the one pinned, a red banner
in that conversation and no badge until you choose "trust the new one"; nothing is
blocked. Removing clears the profile line at once and offers to delete the gist (one
more sign-in, or Joma opens the gist for you).

- [ ] A:

## C. Backup

# 9. Keeping it current

The archive changes when you add contacts or devices. Proposal: "back up now" always,
plus automatic backups when you turn them on (a push after each such change, with the
refresh token from 4). With them off, a reminder when the backup is older than the last
change.

- [ ] A:

# 10. The password

Already answered. One normal password for all accounts, no word lists. The key comes
from a slow derivation, Joma refuses only obviously weak passwords, and it says plainly
that a forgotten password makes the backup useless.

- [x] A: (User, 2026-11-23: a normal secure password, no word lists; private repo plus a
  good password is enough. One password for all accounts.)

# 11. What is in it, and which accounts

Proposal: accounts only (key, contacts, username, devices, settings), not the
conversation history, which is much bigger and comes back from contacts anyway. You
choose per account; agent accounts are listed too, off by default. Joma refuses to write
into a repo that is public.

- [ ] A:

## D. New machines

# 12. One screen for a fresh install

Proposal: the first-start screen offers *create*, *link from another device*, and
*restore from GitHub*. Restore: sign in → Joma lists the accounts in `index.json` → you
tick which ones → you type the password once → the accounts come back with the same Jami
IDs, so contacts, usernames and badges stay valid. Also in the accounts tab ("add →
restore from GitHub") and as `joma restore`.

- [ ] A:

# 13. Adding a machine while the old one works

Restoring signs a new device certificate, so the backup also adds a machine without the
two-device link code; both machines then sync as usual. Proposal: the same restore flow,
worded "add this machine from your backup" when the account still has devices. Every
other device then shows "new device *desktop* joined from the backup · keep / revoke"
(`KnownDevicesChanged`). A link code is never approved from GitHub.

- [ ] A:

# 14. After a restore or a new device

Linking drops the profile line (see above). Proposal: whenever a device starts on an
account that your `joma.json` already lists, Joma puts the line back by itself, with no
new GitHub sign-in. Folder sync (its own discussion) picks up from there too.

- [ ] A:

## E. Agent and command line

# 15. The commands

Each step lands together with its command, so the agent can do everything the window
does. The commands talk to the running Joma over its socket, like `joma send` today; if
Joma isn't running (a fresh install), the command starts it hidden. All take `--json`
and exit non-zero on failure.

```
joma github connect [--gh]       sign in: prints the code and github.com/login/device,
                                 waits for your approval (or uses gh's login)
joma github status               signed in, badge per account, last backup, automatic on/off
joma github badge on|off [ACCT]  publish or withdraw the gist entry and the profile line
joma github disconnect           drop the token; offers to delete the gist and the repo
joma backup [ACCT…|--all]        push now
joma backup auto on|off
joma backup list                 what joma-backup holds (from index.json)
joma restore [ACCT…|--all] [--file PATH]
                                 restore, or add this machine; from GitHub or a file
joma lookup gh:alice             read alice's joma.json: logins, labels, Jami IDs
joma add gh:alice[/label]        check, then send the contact request
joma devices                     this account's devices; joma devices revoke ID
```

Proposal: these names, `ACCT` being a label, a username or a Jami ID as in
`joma account`. Missing anything?

- [ ] A:

# 16. Secrets and approvals stay with you

An agent runs the commands, but two things never go through it. **The password:**
`joma backup` and `joma restore` ask for it in Joma's own window, never on a command line,
in an environment variable or through a pipe, because transcripts and logs keep it. The
command waits and reports only "done" or "wrong password". **The GitHub approval:**
`joma github connect` prints the code; you approve it in your browser. Proposal: that,
plus a terminal prompt instead of the window when you run the command yourself in a
terminal (Joma can tell: a real tty and no agent environment). Or always the window?

- [ ] A:

# 17. What the agent may do on its own

Proposal: the agent may run every command above without asking, except `restore` on a
machine that already has accounts, `github disconnect` and `devices revoke`, which it
should confirm with you first (this goes in the agent's instructions, which Joma can
install with the agent account; see the agents discussion). Should it also warn when a
backup is old, or check `joma github status` from time to time?

- [ ] A:

## F. Safety

# 18. What each thing protects, stated plainly

Proposal for the help text and the setup screen:

- The gist is public: anyone can see that your GitHub account owns these Jami accounts.
  That is the point of the badge; leave the badge off for an account you keep separate.
- Someone with your GitHub account can change the gist. Contacts who already trust you
  see the red banner (pinning) rather than a silent switch.
- Someone with your GitHub account gets the encrypted backup, and needs the password too.
  Whoever has both holds the account key. Revoking stops one device, but they can make
  another, so a leaked backup plus password means moving to a new Jami account.
- Turning it all off: revoke the app on GitHub, delete the gist and the repo. Joma offers
  each step.

- [ ] A:

## G. Order

# 19. Order of building

Proposal:

1. `joma backup` / `joma restore` with `gh` and an encrypted file, and `joma github status`:
   no app needed, and the agent path works from day one.
2. Restore and "add this machine" on the first-start screen, the keep / revoke notice.
3. The badge and adding by GitHub name, with `gh` or by hand (Joma copies `joma.json`
   and opens gist.github.com).
4. The GitHub App with the device flow, for people without `gh`.
5. Automatic backups.

Each step with its commands from section E and their tests.

- [ ] A:
